Fluoride in GAC and gas phase was measured (µg/g for carbon, ppm(v) for gas) to track inorganic fluoride formation during reactivation, which supports assessment of PFAS defluorination but specific extents are not reported in the inspected text.

Thermal reactivation restored the PFAS-laden GAC to a near-virgin state suitable for reuse, implying substantial recovery of adsorption capacity, though no quantitative capacity recovery or cycle number is reported in the inspected text.
endpoints.reported_term: GAC reactivation / restoration to near-virgin state

limitations.statement: Evidence available is from a single full-scale reactivation facility using a multihearth furnace with appropriate off-gas abatement; results may not generalize to other furnace designs or facilities without similar abatement systems.

endpoints.interpretation: Hydrated lime additive is reported to decrease the temperature and time required to mineralize PFAS in PFOS-loaded GAC during thermal treatment; the study itself models the implications of these experimental findings for life cycle impacts rather than directly measuring mineralization.

Using hydrated lime decreases environmental impact in all LCA categories relative to non-additive thermal treatment, attributed to lower temperature/time requirements for PFAS mineralization and avoidance of post-processes for VOF and HF.

limitations.statement: The improved performance with hydrated lime is evaluated through LCA modelling that relies on prior experimental information about PFAS mineralization behavior, rather than new measurements of mineralization extent or kinetics.

comparability.reason: Only qualitative PFAS destruction and media-change information is available from the abstract; no quantified destruction efficiencies, energy use, or reagent consumption are reported, limiting comparison with other regeneration technologies.

endpoints.interpretation: Extent of PFAS destruction on spent GAC during hydrothermal alkaline treatment; abstract states HALT is applied "to destroy PFAS" but does not quantify destruction efficiency.

Analyses of reactor liquid products, media mass loss, and NaOH neutralization suggest removal of co-adsorbed organics and surface carbon gasification analogous to thermal reactivation, indicating change in GAC properties relevant for regeneration.
endpoints.reported_term: removal of adsorbed non-target organic matter and possible GAC surface renewal

limitations.statement: Hydrothermal alkaline treatment conditions and PFAS destruction are reported only as example temperature, pressure, and qualitative destruction; no quantitative destruction or defluorination extents are visible in the abstract.
The HALT regeneration results appear to be based on spent GAC from a single long-term PFAS treatment field pilot source, which may limit generalizability to other spent media or contaminant mixtures.
